history.summary:

Principal Shakti Peetha on Nilachal Hill, Guwahati, and centre of Tantric Shakta worship. The site is one of the 51 Shakti Peethas, where the yoni of Sati is believed to have fallen. The present temple was rebuilt in 1565 under the Koch king Nara Narayan (1540-1587), supervised by his brother Chilarai, reusing material from the earlier ruined temple; earlier destruction is now attributed to Hussein Shah's 1498 invasion rather than Kalapahar. The Ahom kings later patronised and added to the temple (e.g. the natamandapa by Rajeshwar Singha). The sanctum has no idol: a natural cleft in rock, kept filled with spring water, is worshipped as the goddess. CSV town 'Dispur' corrected to Guwahati (Dispur is within the Guwahati circuit area; the temple is at Kamakhya, Nilachal Hill).

town_description: Guwahati is the largest city of Assam and the principal city of Northeast India, on the south bank of the Brahmaputra. Once the seat of the ancient kingdom of Pragjyotishpura/Kamarupa, it is the region's main commercial and transport hub and a centre of Shakti worship, with Kamakhya, Umananda and Ugratara shrines.
